On January 14, 1916, Tom died at Brooklyn, New York, and his remains were interred in Pine Lake Cemetery just north of LaPorte, Indiana. Tom and his brother, Turner W. source_description: Melvin Albert (Bert) Weed (1882-1964) began in the pharmacy business in 1898 as a clerk at the Bartell Drug Company. After college he partnered with Albert G. Keene (1854-1924) and worked as a pharmacist at Lake Washington Pharmacy. In 1906, Bert married Keene's daughter Mamie Luella Keene (1881-1970), and they had one daughter, Luell (Weed) Guthrie (1910-1987). Lake Washington Pharmacy became Weed's Pharmacy in 1910, operating in the same Central District location until Bert's retirement in 1958. The Weed family was well-known in the Seattle community thanks to Bert's involvement in many community associations, including the Freemasons, the Nile Temple, and the Sons of the American Revolution. source_description: Title Business card advertising Forrest, Jones & Co. as "Dealers in Slaves" Description Located at No. 89 Adams Street, Memphis, Tennessee, the owners of this slave-dealing business included Nathan Bedford Forrest, later a famous Confederate general during the Civil War, and his brother William. The bottom of the business card reads, "They will Board and Sell on Commission, and keep constantly on hand, a good assortment of Virginia, Georgia, and Carolina Negroes for sale." On the reverse of the card is written in pencil, "Sold Madison to Forrest," possibly referring to an enslaved person sold to Forrest by the owner of Belle Meade plantation near Nashville. Four enslaved individuals were killed in this brick building on Jan. 13, 1860 when it collapsed following heavy rains; Forrest, one of Memphis' largest slave dealers and wealthiest men, closed the business soon afterwards....

Hindu symbols were used by Badische Anilin & Soda-Fabrik (BASF) on their company's dye labels because India was one of the earliest producers of indigo dye. BASF began the industrial production of synthetic indigo in 1897. The decorative border includes the BASF trademark insignia. Founded in 1865, Badische Anilin & Soda-Fabrik (BASF) was once the largest chemical factory in the world. Based in Ludwigshafen, Germany, the company first concentrated on the manufacture of synthetic dyestuffs. source_description: Sketch for a humorous "trade card" (combination advertisement and business card) for one Théophile Belin (whose first name is ornamentally spelled with a Greek letter Theta), drawn by French caricaturist Adolphe Willette ca. 1900. Probably the actual printed cards would have contained additional text, otherwise it would be a "visiting card" (there is no address or profession marked). This jocularly depicts a medieval young woman confined in a chastity belt (though as a matter of historical fact the chastity belt was much more of a Renaissance phenomenon than medieval), and also a highly-caricatured pseudo-medieval man with a ring of keys who has entered by climbing a ladder to the balcony outside her window. The woman is drawn as quite cheerful, despite wearing nothing but her voluminous hair-covering headdress and the chastity belt...

source_description: French-language advertisement for the beauty and health institute at No. 14 Franklin Street, Bucharest, Romania. The founder and owner is Leone Friedman, "Member of the Dermatological and Syphiligraphic Society, Paris. Former attending physician in the Skin Disease and Syphilis Clinic at the Universities of Berlin and Florence. Former assistant to Professor [Camillo] Golgi, a laureate of the international Nobel Prize." Friedman promised: the "pain-free treatment" of acne, alopecia, birthmarks, blackheads, port-wine stains and rosacea; the removal of scars or moles; depilation; the non-surgical "correction of deformed noses"; the X-ray treatment of lupus, "from the method devised by Professor [Niels Ryberg] Finsen"; and "the most modern installation for for the radical cure of skin, venereal and syphilitic diseases."

source_description: Color print advertisement for Dow Plastics. The advertisement shows a composite illustration of historical figures, include a glassblower, two figures in the style of ancient Egyptian art, and a man in a lab coat working with machinery. The accompanying text traces the change over time in the meaning of the word "plastic," from an adjective to a noun used for a specific material. The text also describes the different qualities of several Dow plastic products, including Saran, Styron and Ethocel. This advertisement appeared on the inside cover of the March 27, 1944 edition of Newsweek. It is part of a series of advertisements titled "Five Minute Forum on Plastics." Notably, the advertisement was produced during World War II and bears the Company's wartime tagline "Dow: Chemicals Indispensable to Industry and Victory."

source_collection: This photograph was made publicly available in the United States on 1 June 1951 as a Press Photo without a visible copyright notice. A scanned copy can be found at worthpoint.com . It is also available online by Getty Images via ullstein bild Dtl and Bettmann archives.
source_description: Iran (General). Tehran, Iran. Above is one of the Anti-American posters carried in the big parade of 100,000 workers and peasants. Staged last Tuesday in Tehran by the supposedly outlawed Tudeh party (Communist Party of Iran). The Tudeh now operates under the guise of the "peace movement" and the "organization for the nationalization ..." This banner depicts Uncle Sam being thrown out of Iran. The legend of the banner says that American "junk sellers" import 200,000 tons of preservatives and 1,000,000 dolls, etc., into the country. Today President Truman appealed to Iran Premier Mossadegh to negotiate with Britain on nationalization of the Anglo-Iranian oil fields.

source_description: ADVERTISEMENT FOR THE DIAL A RIDE RADIO DISPATCHED DOOR-TO-DOOR BUS SERVICE IN HADDONFIELD, NEW JERSEY. IT BEGAN IN FEBRUARY, 1972, AS A DEMONSTRATION PROJECT BETWEEN FEDERAL AND STATE TRANSPORTATION DEPARTMENTS. FUNDING ENDED IN MARCH, 1975 SPOKESMEN REPORTED THE SYSTEM WORKED WELL IN RUSH HOUR ALONG FIXED ROUTES. BUT THE FARE WASN'T ENOUGH TO COVER ONE TO THREE PERSONS PICKED UP AT HOME IN OFF HOURS. source_description: Building of the Alfred Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI) with a poster mounted to its western wall. The poster installation is part of the art project 'POLARFRONT' which was performed by Birgit Mieding, Johannes Freitag & Ingo Sikorski during the Year of the Geosciences in 2005 in cooperation with the AWI and the German Maritime Museum (DSM), both Bremerhaven, Germany. The project consisted of four large posters with photos from the Antarctic of which three were mounted to the walls of AWI and DSM and one installed in the river Weser.

source_description: Die Evolution der Tiere: Das Poster zeigt im oberen Teil Entstehung der Erde und Lebens mit der Verzweigung in die Hauptevolutionslinien des Tierreiches. Pilze, Pflanzen, Algen (Protoctista) und Bakterien sind im oberen Bereich als Seitenzweige der frühen Evolution dargestellt. Die Evolution der Tiere geht von vielzelligen Organismen aus, die durch interne Kompartimentierung und Bildung von Kollagen als formstabilisierendes Material entstanden sind, die sogenannten Gallertoide. Diese sind von einem cilienbesetzten Kanalsystem durchzogen. Ausgehend von diesen frühen Tieren entwickelten sich mehrere Hauptlinien, die sich schließlich in die weiteren Hauptevolutionslinien differenzierten. source_description: Atacamite Locality: Collahuasi Mine, Collahuasi district, Iquique Province , Tarapacá Region , Chile ( Locality at mindat.org ) Size: 6.4 x 5.2 x 3.8 cm. This is a complexly intergrown mass of crystallized atacamite, in huge crystals unlike any I have seen from Chile. It is 100% crystals. I have never myself seen another specimen from this remote copper mine located 170 km SE of Iquique. source_description: Information Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud presided over an inter-ministerial meeting held in the ministry's conference room in Dhaka. The meeting focused on bringing various aspects of social media and OTT (Over-the-Top) platforms under regulatory frameworks, including the display of foreign content in Bangladesh, the display and advertisement of various Bangladeshi content, and bringing them under the purview of taxation. The meeting aimed to regulate and bring these practices under the tax net. The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications, Mustafa Jabbar, and the State Minister for Information, Dr. Md. Murad Hasan, participated in the meeting online. The meeting took place on Sunday, July 5, 2020.
